To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Colloid science is a powerful tool to understand and manipulate the dynamics of phase transition processes.

(i) the dynamics of phase transition is governed by a complex interplay of thermodynamics and kinetics, (ii) the kinetics is controlled by the competition between attractive interactions, which promote ordering and phase transitions, and repulsive interactions, which prevent ordering, and (iii) the dynamics of ordering can be described using a general model, which is applicable to a wide range of different systems.

(1) Colloids display a wide range of phase transitions, including gas, liquid, crystal, and liquid crystalline transitions; (2) Colloids can become trapped in metastable states; (3) The phase diagram is not always realized; (4) The phase diagram can be influenced by the presence of impurities, such as surfactants or ions.
